en: The Buddha-ūṣṇīṣa-parama-siddhi-dhāraṇī Sūtra, translated by the Tripitaka Master Divākara of India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
He was accompanied by a great assembly of eight thousand bhikṣus,
as well as bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others,
all of whom had attained the bright torch of correct wisdom.
They illumined all dharmas without any obstruction.
Their names were: Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, Padmottaragarbha Bodhisattva, Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin Bodhisattva, and Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas such as Mahāsthāmaprāpta, Vajrapāṇi, Gaganagañja, Samantabhadra, Maitreya, and Kṣitigarbha.
Thus, these thirty-two thousand foremost disciples were present together with them.
Furthermore, ten thousand Brahmā kings, such as the Deva Sata,
each came from other worlds to the place where the Buddha was.
Furthermore, twelve thousand Śakras,
together with immeasurable devas, nāgas, the eight classes of beings, humans, and non-humans, came to where the Buddha was. At that time,
the World-Honored One was surrounded by the fourfold assembly.
They made offerings and paid him respect as he preached the Dharma.
At that time, among the host of Śakra-devānām-indra,
there was a deva named Sunetra.
Dwelling in a great jewel palace with various celestial maidens,
he indulged in heedless play and enjoyed pleasures at his will.
During that night, a voice called out to Sthira, saying:
"Seven days from now your life will surely end.
You will undergo seven cycles of birth and death in Jambudvīpa,
after which you shall again enter hell."
After emerging from hell, he obtained a human body;
however, born blind and impoverished, he underwent all manner of suffering.
Upon hearing this, Śubhavyūha was struck with alarm and fell into a state of terror.
With the hair on his body standing on end and trembling with anxiety,
he rushed to the abode of that Śakra-devendra,
recounted what he had heard, and entreated him for compassionate rescue.
At that time, Śakra, King of the Devas, having heard the words of Sudṛḍha, felt a surge of alarm and sorrow, and reflected silently to himself:
"What manner of beings are those seven births? To what class do they belong?"
Having formed this thought, he immediately saw that Sthira was manifesting the signs of death and receiving the body of a pig;
having finished his life as a pig, he would again receive the body of a dog.
In this sequence, he was born as a fox,
a monkey, a venomous snake, a crow, and a vulture;
for seven such lifetimes, he constantly consumed foul and impure things.
At that time, having witnessed this event, Śakra, King of the Devas,
felt deep compassion for Shan-zhu (Susthitamati), realizing he would surely suffer such misery;
he thought to himself that there was nothing he could do for him.
Only the Buddha, the World-Honored One, is able to provide salvation. Then,
during the latter part of the night,
the Heavenly King Śakra brought various flower garlands, garments, necklaces, and all kinds of incense.
He went to the kingdom of Śrāvastī to make offerings to the World-Honored One.
Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, he withdrew to stand to one side and addressed the Buddha, saying: “World-Honored One.”
In the palace where I reside, there was a devaputra named Sunetra.
He was addicted to idle pleasures and spent his time wandering about according to his own whims.
One night, a voice suddenly called out to him, saying:
Seven days from now, your life will certainly come to an end.
You shall undergo the retribution of the seven evils in Jambudvīpa;
wherever you are born, you will constantly consume foul and impure things.
From that point onward, they will again enter hell.
Emerging from hell, they will be born among humans,
where they will experience all manner of sufferings, such as blindness, poverty, and destitution.
They sought refuge with me, but there was nothing I could do;
I thought only that the World-Honored One could save them.
At that time, the World-Honored One heard and perceived the request made by Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having finished his petition.
From the crown of his head, he emitted various multicolored rays of light that flowed forth,
illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions; having shone upon them,
they returned to the presence of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] three times, it entered through the Buddha’s mouth.
The Buddha then smiled and addressed Śakradevendra, saying:
"I possess such a pure, supreme Great Dhāraṇī for consecrating all realms of existence."
It can fulfill your wishes, rescue them from suffering,
and bring great benefit to all sentient beings. O Lord of Devas,
such is the power of this divine mantra of mine.
It can extinguish all karmic obstructions and the various sufferings of the hells, the animal realm, Yama, and so forth;
it can also destroy the paths leading to the hells and other such realms.
It causes all sentient beings to set out upon the path to perfect enlightenment.
O Lord of Devas, if there are those who can hear it even for a moment,
they shall all completely eliminate all karmic obstructions and the various sufferings of birth and death.
They shall obtain great benefit and attain the knowledge of past lives;
they shall go from one buddha-field to another buddha-field,
and be reborn from one celestial realm into another celestial realm.
In whatever place one is born, one will always remember past lives.
If there are those who study this sutra and its dhāraṇī,
their lifespan, though limited to a hundred years, shall be further increased.
Their body, speech, and mind are pure, and they dwell in serene peace and happiness.
All Buddhas gaze upon them, all devas protect them,
and all Bodhisattvas bestow their compassionate thoughts upon them.
If one constantly reads and recites this sutra and its dhāraṇī,
all the sufferings within the three evil realms will be extinguished and cease to manifest.
All the celestial gates of merit in every buddha-field shall guide them to enter therein.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having heard the Buddha’s praise and exposition of this dhāraṇī,
came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
we pray that the Tathāgata will out of compassion take pity upon and protect all sentient beings."
"Please proclaim the most supreme Great Dharani of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa, which purifies all realms of existence as you have described.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having accepted the request of Śakra,
the Lord of Devas, immediately expounded the dharani, saying:
Namo namo tathāgatāya bhagavate jvala-locana-pratibhāsiṣṭha-khecarāya yathā-sambuddhāya mahāmune tadyathā oṃ hūṃ vidhūtaye svāhā. (3)

Vibhūte vibhūte (43) buddhaye buddhaye (44) samantamukhe dharmadhātu-parivartini (45) sarvatathāgata-ādhiṣṭhāna-ādhiṣṭhite (46) svāhā (47).
The Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas:
"This dhāraṇī has been proclaimed by eighty-eight billion hundred-thousand Ganges-sands of Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones;
it is guarded, praised, and sealed with the seal of wisdom."
In this way, these Buddhas, desiring to liberate those submerged in the ocean of suffering and the poisons of misery— such as those in the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of Yama—
and furthermore wishing to benefit those of short lifespan, meager merit, and lowly or base status, [act accordingly].
Because all sentient beings have various evil karmas;
and because they seek peaceful rebirths in the various evil realms, yet meet with untimely death and distracted minds;
and because all sentient beings suffer from various afflictions.
For this reason, the Buddhas have taught this most supreme great dhāraṇī.
O Devendra, you should now bestow this great dhāraṇī upon the deva Suvihita, so that he may practice it.
Furthermore, you should also proclaim and expound it for those sons of the gods in heaven, as well as for all sentient beings in Jambudvīpa,
causing those beings to receive, uphold, read, and recite it.
Make offerings, show reverence, honor, and praise it.
O Lord of Devas, I entrust this dharma-dhāraṇī-mudrā to you;
you should uphold it with devotion.
Those who uphold this mantra will be able to completely eliminate all karmic offenses from hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Wherever they are born, they will always encounter the Buddhas,
until they finally attain unsurpassed bodhi.
"O Lord of Devas, this Dharma-seal Great Dhāraṇī possesses great auspiciousness.
Just as the place where a jewel from the Sun-Treasury (Sūryagarbha) resides is brilliantly illuminated,
it is also like the gold of Jambudvīpa."
It is without defilement, without blemish, and unstained by dust or grime.
If there are those who can read, recite, copy, uphold, remember, practice,
and make offerings to it, [they shall attain such merit].
One shall fully obtain all the merits mentioned above.
O Lord of Devas, if one were to write down this great dhāraṇī and install it upon a tall banner placed on a high mountain, [the merit would be immeasurable].
Whether on a high roof, a lofty place, or within a high tower,
those among the fourfold assembly who see [this] from afar or nearby shall likewise obtain all the merits mentioned above.
Sometimes the shadow of the banner covers their bodies;
sometimes they are buffeted by the wind from the banner;
and sometimes flying dust from the fluttering banner settles upon them.
They shall also obtain all the merits mentioned above. O Śakra,
if there are members of the fourfold assembly who are able to construct stūpas and temples at various crossroads, they shall likewise obtain such merit.
Having installed such a great dhāraṇī,
one should daily make offerings with various flower garlands, silk banners,
flags, canopies, necklaces, incense, and so forth.
Furthermore, those who are able to circumambulate, pay respect to,
and prostrate before [this] should be known as great bodhisattvas;
they are true sons of the Buddha and bridges of the Dharma.
It is also a precious stūpa containing the relics of all the Buddhas.
At that time, when the Dharma King Yama heard of this matter,
it was toward dawn.
Carrying various multicolored jewel flowers,
diverse incenses, precious robes, and necklaces,
they came to the place where the Buddha was and prostrated at his feet.
Having circumambulated [the Buddha] seven times, he withdrew to stand to one side.
Having made offerings to the Tathāgata with various ritual implements and completed his worship, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
Now, desiring to repay the Buddha's kindness,
I shall constantly and diligently serve this one of great majesty and great retribution,
who protects all beings and closes the gates of hell.
The Great Dhāraṇī for Purifying All Realms of Existence.
At that time, the Four Heavenly Kings rose from their seats,
circumambulated the Buddha three times, and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One, we pray that you will explain for us this method for practicing the dhāraṇī.
The Buddha told the Four Heavenly Kings, “Listen attentively, listen attentively, and reflect upon it well.
For your sakes and for the sake of all sentient beings, I shall do so.”
I shall now explain the dharma for practicing this dhāraṇī.
If there are those whose lives are short and who seek longevity,
or those who suffer from illness and seek recovery;
Or there may be those with evil karma who ought to fall into the various unwholesome realms such as the hells, hungry ghosts, or animals;
all such individuals shall, on the fifteenth day of that month, [be purified].
Having bathed for purification and put on fresh, clean garments,
one should further observe the eightfold precepts of the fast;
thereafter, recite this great dhāraṇī one thousand times in full.
They shall obtain peace and happiness and increase their lifespan;
all illnesses and sufferings shall be healed and cured,
and all karmic retributions for evil deeds shall be extinguished without remainder.
If there are those who hear this mantra with their ears, they shall,
for the remainder of their lives, go to the Land of Ultimate Bliss,
be born by transformation within a lotus flower, and always possess the knowledge of past lives.
If there are those who have already passed away, having been drawn by such evil karma,
one should likewise recite this dhāraṇī mantra twenty-one times and scatter consecrated earth over their remains.
Wherever they are reborn, they shall cast off that suffering body and be born in the heavens to enjoy bliss.
If one can recite this most supreme Great Dhāraṇī Sūtra twenty-one times every day, [the aforementioned benefits shall be attained].
They shall also attain all the aforementioned merits;
in every birth, they will always dwell in pure Buddha-lands and manifest great radiance throughout all Buddha-fields.
They shall always be with the Buddha and receive his prediction [of enlightenment],
until they attain Great Parinirvāṇa.
If there are any persons who, regarding this Dharma-gate...
Regarding the various aspirations and vows sought as described above,
one should construct a square altar, perfectly regular in its four sides.
Within that altar, one should scatter various kinds of flowers and burn many varieties of renowned incense.
With single-minded devotion, universally bring to mind all Buddhas of the ten directions.
Kneel with the right knee touching the ground, join the palms,
and bend the two index fingers to press against the two thumbs.
One should inwardly exclaim "Excellent!
upon one's heart, and then recite this dhāraṇī mantra.
If there is anyone who can recite and uphold this mantra...
If one recites this one hundred and eight times every day,
it shall constitute an offering to all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges mentioned above,
and it shall likewise constitute an offering to you, the Four Kings.
One should know that all praise is well-bestowed upon such a person;
for having adorned their mind with great bodhi and attained unimpeded wisdom, they are a true son of the Buddha.
At that time, after the World-Honored One had spoken these words,
he addressed the Lord of Devas, saying:
"Lord of Devas, you may take this dharma of the dhāraṇī."
Having instructed him to remain well-settled for seven full days,
he was to come to my presence together with him. Then,
having received the Buddha’s instruction, the King of the Śakras returned to his own celestial palace.
He called forth Śubhavyūha and bestowed that divine mantra upon him. Having heard it, Śubhavyūha paid respectful homage and practiced according to the instructions for seven days.
Consequently, all his evil karmas were completely eliminated.
Their lifespan increased within that very heaven, and they leaped for joy, crying out in a great voice:
"How wonderful is the Buddha! How wonderful is the Dharma! How wonderful is the Saṅgha!"
How marvelous is the power of this supreme dhāraṇī-seal!
It can extinguish all suffering and calamity,
enabling me to be liberated from such evil karma.
At that time, having witnessed this event, the Deva Sthira went to where the Lord of Devas was and spoke these words:
"I have received the grace of the gods; please request the Buddha on my behalf."
The Buddha has taught me a great dhāraṇī,
which has caused all my evil karma to be completely extinguished.
I wish to go and express my gratitude for the kindness of the Buddha, the World-Honored One.
"I only pray that the Heavenly King will go with me.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, together with his various retinues,
accompanied by Sunanda, took up various fragrant flowers and many exquisite necklaces.
Riding in a celestial precious carriage, he proceeded to the place where the Buddha was.
There, he made offerings to the Tathāgata with various ritual implements,
circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, and stood to one side.
The virtues of the Buddha were sung in praise beyond the power of words to express.
At that time, the World-Honored One extended his golden hand,
stroked the head of that Well-Established One, and with a harmonious and elegant voice, bestowed upon him the prediction of enlightenment.
Then the deva Susthita, filled with joy, withdrew to sit down and listened to the essential teachings of the Dharma expounded by the Tathāgata.
Having heard the teaching, his heart leaped with exultation.
Together with the Lord of Devas, they prostrated before the Buddha and withdrew.
The *Buddhapiṭaka-uttama-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, the *Mahācakra-vajra-dhāraṇī*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīlabhadra by imperial decree. *Namo satvāya*.
Dhīḥ vikaraṇa-tathāgatān oṃ vilokaya vilokaya mahākāra.
Vajrī sata sata sarati sarati taraye.
Tāriye vidamane saṃpanaye.
Tāramati-siddha-ajalidhyāna.

*Svāhā*. If one recites this *dhāraṇī* twenty-one times, one shall immediately enter all maṇḍala altars; whatever is performed will be accomplished. Regarding the recitation of mantras, there are bodily mudrās and hand mudrās; if one performs these mudrās while reciting the mantra according to the ritual method, success is easily attained. However, if one has not yet entered the altar, one must not perform them recklessly. By reciting this mantra, one shall then be able to enter the altar, perform the mudrās, and apply them in practice; it is not a case of stealing the dharma.

The Mantra of the Bodhisattva Sūryaprabha: *Namo buddhāya gurave | namo dharmāya mahate | namaḥ saṃghāya tāyine |* Reciting this mantra extinguishes all obstacles and can also ward off demons and eliminate celestial calamities. Furthermore, if one recites it once and performs one prostration to the Buddha, doing so three times each day, one will in the future obtain the karmic fruit of having two marks of physical perfection and being endowed with beauty. *Oṃ māriciye sarvasattvārthakarī śrīsvāhā |* Reciting this mantra provides supreme protection for the human body; one should recite it one hundred and eight times during each of the three periods of the day.
